title: Terminal Internacional T2 — FINAL v2
subtitle: LATAM Counter — Systemic Denial & 'Passa Diario' Admission
location: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCL) — Terminal 2 (T2), LATAM Check-In Counter, airside
classification: Attorney Work Product — Privileged and Confidential

cluster_A_dgac_validation.summary: DGAC official Nicolás validates passenger's rights: the airline must solve the problem, rebook at no cost, and the passenger has sufficient evidence for a complaint. Nicolás acknowledges the passenger's account ('yo te entiendo completamente') but explains DGAC cannot provide written documentation, setting the stage for LATAM's refusal.
cluster_A_dgac_validation.reasoning: Nicolás, a DGAC official, independently confirms key points: 'ellos te tienen que solucionar el problema', 'ellos te lo tienen que reprogramar', and 'tú tienes todos los antecedentes que necesitas como para hacer un reclamo.' He explicitly states he does not dispute the passenger's version ('Si! yo no le pongo en discussion'). However, he disclaims DGAC's ability to issue documentation: 'nosotros no te lo vamos a poder dar porque no es como materia competente de nosotros.' This establishes the documentary vacuum — no institution at the airport will provide written documentation. Nicolás gives his name, making him a potential witness.
provisions_engaged: CACH Art. 133 (carrier obligations)
LPDC Art. 23 bis (written notice — foreshadowing violation)
cluster_A_dgac_validation.violation_linkage: Establishes baseline: DGAC validates passenger's rights but cannot enforce documentation, creating the vacuum later exploited by LATAM.

cluster_B_disruptivo_label_first_refusal.summary: LATAM counter staff inform passenger he has been classified as 'pasajero disruptivo' in the system, a label applied despite PDI camera disproof. The label forecloses all normal counter services and triggers the first security threat when the passenger persists.
cluster_B_disruptivo_label_first_refusal.reasoning: Staff state: 'La compania ya te categorizo como pasagero disruptivo, no va a poder a embarcar com nosotro.' This label is self-executing: once applied, no verification of underlying facts occurs. The passenger had just presented evidence that both accusations were disproven by cameras, yet the label remains. When the passenger presses for written documentation, the staff respond with 'llamo la seguridad para que usted hable con ellos,' initiating a pattern of security threats used to deter rights assertion.
provisions_engaged: CONST Art. 19 N°4 (honor damaged by false label)
Ley 20.609 (arbitrary discrimination)
LPDC Art. 3(1)(b) (no arbitrary discrimination)
CACH Art. 133 (carrier obligations undermined by classification)
cluster_B_disruptivo_label_first_refusal.violation_linkage: F-T2-011 (disruptivo classification without verification), CL-001 (false accusation), CL-035 (discrimination), pattern of security threats.

cluster_C_no_existe_documentary_denial.summary: CRITICAL: LATAM staff categorically state that written documentation does not exist at the airport: 'QUE ALGO POR ESCRITO NO EXISTE… ACA EN EL AEROPUERTO NO SE ENTREGA.' The only path offered is to demand through the airline's lawyers.
cluster_C_no_existe_documentary_denial.reasoning: This is the core documentary admission. Staff explicitly declare: 'QUE ALGO POR ESCRITO NO EXISTE… NO EXISTE.. ACA EN EL AEROPUERTO NO SE ENTREGA.' When the passenger asks how to obtain it, the response is 'LO TIENE QUE PEDIR A LOS ABOGADOS DE LA EMPRESA' — an impossible circular requirement. This is a categorical institutional policy: no passenger removed from a flight will ever receive written documentation at SCL airport, directly violating mandatory written notice requirements under LPDC Art. 23 bis. The 'NO EXISTE' assertion is later contradicted (see cluster H) when staff admit the security chief can produce a 'comprobante,' confirming documentation exists but is systematically withheld.
provisions_engaged: LPDC Art. 23 bis (mandatory written notice — direct breach)
LPDC Art. 3(1)(d) (right to truthful and timely information)
LPDC Art. 12 (professionalism — categorical refusal)
CACH Art. 133(1) (documentation presupposed by statutory scheme)
CONST Art. 19 N°3 (due process negated by documentary vacuum)
cluster_C_no_existe_documentary_denial.violation_linkage: F-T2-001 (systemic admission of 'NO EXISTE' as corporate policy), CL-038 (LPDC Art. 23 bis breach), CL-018 (institutionalized evasion), CL-037 (professionalism), CL-011 (due process).

cluster_D_total_blockade_security_threat.summary: LATAM staff impose a total service blockade, declaring that no employee will assist the passenger and that he can only speak with security ('solamente puede hablar CON SEGURIDAD'). Three security threats are issued when the passenger persists in requesting documentation.
cluster_D_total_blockade_security_threat.reasoning: After the 'NO EXISTE' denial, the staff systematically block all channels: 'acá no te puedo ayudar,' 'lo que tú estás pidiendo no corresponde — no se emite de ninguna manera.' When the passenger continues, the staff escalate to a full blockade: 'ya nadie va a poder hacer una gestión contigo, solamente puede hablar CON SEGURIDAD.' The pattern of security threats (segs 72, 87, 109) demonstrates that the institutional response to rights assertion is intimidation, not service. The passenger is effectively excluded from all normal commercial channels.
provisions_engaged: LPDC Art. 3(1)(b) (no arbitrary discrimination — exclusion from service)
Ley 20.609 (exclusion from public accommodation)
CONST Art. 19 N°3 (exclusion without due process)
CACH Art. 133 (carrier duties converted to exclusion)
cluster_D_total_blockade_security_threat.violation_linkage: F-T2-005 (total service block), F-T2-010 (security threat pattern), CL-035, CL-018, CL-011, TOTAL-SERVICE-BLOCK.

cluster_E_facts_irrelevant_no_se_va_disc.summary: LATAM staff declare that whether the accusations were true or false is irrelevant and will not be discussed ('No se va discutir si tu fuiste o no'). Staff admit the company has no solutions for passengers labeled 'disruptivo' ('La empresa no tiene ninguna solución para casos cuando el pasajero queda como disruptivo'). Staff also exhibit the personal/institutional split: 'Como persona yo te entiendo... pero.'
cluster_E_facts_irrelevant_no_se_va_disc.reasoning: This cluster reveals the procedural DNA of the system. The staff explicitly state: 'No se va discutir si tu fuiste o no lo hicieste' — the truth is excluded from the procedural framework. The passenger's protest that both accusations were disproven by PDI cameras is met with 'no se va a estar discutiendo.' Additionally, staff admit 'La empresa no tiene ninguna solución para casos cuando el pasajero queda como disruptivo' — there is zero corrective mechanism by design. The statement 'Como persona yo te entiendo... pero' encapsulates the bureaucratic alienation: personal empathy exists but cannot be translated into institutional action.
provisions_engaged: CONST Art. 19 N°3 (due process — right to be heard)
CONST Art. 19 N°14 (right to petition)
ACHR Art. 8 (right to be heard)
ACHR Art. 25 (simple and prompt recourse)
CACH Art. 133 (lawful process requires factual determination)
LPDC Art. 12 (professionalism negated by 'no se va discutir')
cluster_E_facts_irrelevant_no_se_va_disc.violation_linkage: F-T2-002 (facts irrelevant), F-T2-004 (no solutions admission), CL-011, CL-007, CL-018, PATTERN-OF-FAILURE.

cluster_F_passa_diario_daily_pattern.summary: LATAM staff reveal the systemic scale: 'Passa diario, y siempre la línea aérea va a tener... de ganar aca con la policia' — this happens daily and the airline always wins with the police. Staff then contradict earlier denials by admitting the security chief can produce a 'comprobante.'
cluster_F_passa_diario_daily_pattern.reasoning: This is the climactic admission. 'Passa diario' transforms the case from an isolated incident into a daily industrial process. 'Siempre la línea aérea va a tener... de ganar aca con la policia' indicates a structural alliance between the airline and airport police that guarantees outcomes favorable to the airline. The passenger notes that his case is an exception: 'la policía ya sabe de mi caso, la policía ya está de acuerdo.' Finally, the staff's admission that 'el jefe de seguridad te lo puede conseguir' (the security chief can provide a 'comprobante') directly contradicts the earlier 'NO EXISTE' claim, revealing that documentation does exist but is funneled through security channels inaccessible to passengers.
provisions_engaged: CONST Art. 19 N°2 (equality before the law — structural imbalance)
CONST Art. 19 N°3 (systematic due process denial)
ACHR Art. 8, 25 (systematic denial of judicial protection)
LPDC Art. 23 bis (daily statutory violations)
CACH Art. 133 (systematic aviation law violations)
MC99 (systematic circumvention of carrier liability)
cluster_F_passa_diario_daily_pattern.violation_linkage: F-T2-003 (passa diario admission), F-T2-009 (security documentation channel), CL-018, PATTERN-OF-FAILURE, CL-038, CL-011, CL-016.

cluster_G_female_aggression.summary: A female LATAM counter staff member interjects with aggressive dismissal: 'Oii!!', 'ACA NOS DAMOS PAPELES!' — embodying institutional contempt and confirming the policy of zero written documentation.
cluster_G_female_aggression.reasoning: The female staff member's intervention is qualitatively different from the male staff's bureaucratic demeanor. She shouts 'Oii!!' as a dismissive exclamation and aggressively declares 'ACA NOS DAMOS PAPELES!' — 'WE DON'T GIVE PAPERS HERE!' This is not a jurisdictional limitation but an aggressive assertion of institutional policy. The passenger's response — '¿Cómo no? Es una empresa seria' — highlights the contradiction: a serious company would provide documentation.
provisions_engaged: LPDC Art. 12 (professionalism — aggressive treatment)
Ley 20.609 (discriminatory contempt)
CONST Art. 19 N°4 (damage to dignity)

cluster_H_chain_of_command_security_chan.summary: Staff reveal they 'siguen instrucciones' (follow instructions) from above, diffusing individual responsibility. They advise the passenger that pursuing the matter at the airport will go badly ('acá te va a ir mal') and finally admit that the security chief can provide a document, confirming that documentation exists but is withheld from passengers.
cluster_H_chain_of_command_security_chan.reasoning: Staff state 'Nosotros seguimos instrucciones' — indicating the blockade is corporate policy, not individual discretion. The advice 'acá te va a ir mal' is both a threat and a confession that the system is rigged. The final admission that 'el jefe de seguridad te lo puede conseguir' reveals a two-tier documentation system: security can access documents that passengers cannot. This is the same irregular channel used later by supervisor Diego to fabricate the 'carta de desembarque' via Ventas (STG_29).
provisions_engaged: CONST Art. 19 N°3 (chain of command negates individual accountability)
CACH Art. 133 (individualized assessment required)
LPDC Art. 12 (professionalism negated by 'instrucciones')
MC99 (liability circumvention via institutional design)
cluster_H_chain_of_command_security_chan.violation_linkage: F-T2-009 (chain of command and security channel), CL-018, CL-016, INSTRUCTION-FOLLOWING, WRONGFUL-USE-OF-INTERNAL-CHANNEL.
